subject: filecabinet

measured.lineup: the asset is one of A to D in lineup.png beside models/w_gauss.mdl, models/w_oxygen.mdl, models/w_suit.mdl
measured.lineupTest: asked 4 times, each in another order, which of the four was not made by Valve: judges picked D, D, A, C where the asset was C, A, D, C: passed for one of the game's

M1.reason: In all ten views the outline is a plain upright box with three drawer fronts on the front face and a slightly stepped plinth at the base. The front-left and front-right views show the same box with the drawers in the same places. Nothing sticks out or is missing, and the top is flat with a small edge bevel.

M2.reason: Measured size is 28.8 across, 22.6 wide and 62.4 high against the brief's 29, 23 and 62. Each is within 1% of the brief's figure, well inside 15%.

M3.reason: Parts the brief asks for: three drawers, each a raised front panel with a bevelled edge; three handles, painted as dark pulls on each drawer front (front view, clear at the front-left and front-right views); a base plinth. The brief names no claws, teeth, rivets, tabs or round parts, so there is no count to check beyond these. Handles are painted rather than modelled, which the rubric allows when they read clearly, and they do.

M4.reason: Grey painted steel across the box and drawer fronts, with darker blotches that read as grime, as the brief asks. The handles are a darker tone, as a steel pull would be. No region is a colour a player would call a different material.

M5.reason: The grime the brief asks for is there: mottled dark patches on the left, back, right and top faces, and a dirty base. Drawer seams and bevels show in the front views. One faint rectangular line runs down the left-side view and looks like a painted panel edge; it is a small paint point and does not change the outline.

M6.reason: Capped at 2 by the line-up test, as the rubric directs. The four-reading line-up caught the asset once out of four (picks D, D, A, C against asset positions C, A, D, C), which is a pass for one of the game's.

M7.reason: The drawers face front, the cabinet stands upright on its base, and the plinth sits at the origin, as a filing cabinet placed where the old one did would. The brief names no other front, so there is nothing to compare against.

M8.reason: SMAK's check reports no errors. 14 triangles is far below twice the median of Half-Life's props of this kind (238), so the count passes. The bottom, top and back are closed in the below and top views, nothing is inside out, and nothing floats.
